mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through discounted cash flow effects.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 3.0% is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate indicates a tight labor market, boosting corporate hiring and profit margins, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through improved earnings outlooks.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 3.5% is associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1400 thousand units signals weak consumer demand for housing, reducing construction sector activity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth concerns intensify.
failure_condition: HOUST below 1400.0 is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 300 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL above 300.0 is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and decreases in the unemployment rate signal a tightening monetary policy amid a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate investment and consumer spending.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market strength
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.5 and UNRATE < 3.5, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105 and a simultaneous drop in housing starts below 1400 thousand units indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings growth prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 105.0 and HOUST < 1400.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 300), a higher CPIAUCSL reading signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 300), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a lower unemployment rate signals strong wage growth and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved earnings outlooks.
failure_condition: In the tight labor market regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.
